exercise.name: Leg Raise Dragon Flag
aliases: Bench leg raise to dragon flag

reference.title: Leg Raise Dragon Flag
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (leg raise rolling onto the upper back, then a rigid-body lowering from the shoulders)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out on the raise, brace (short hold) at the top, breathe out slowly through the lowering.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, brief brace, 2.5 s down

prescription.tempo: About 2 s up, 0.5 s brace, 2.5-3 s lowering
prescription.progression: Slower lowering, longer pauses part way down, then full dragon flags

cues.text: Lie on the bench, head near one end, and grip the bench behind your head.
Raise the straight legs to vertical, then keep going: roll the hips and low back up off the bench onto the upper back.
At the top, squeeze the glutes and lock the body straight from the shoulders to the toes.
Lower the whole body as one rigid line, slowly, pivoting on the upper back.
Bring the hips down to the bench and the legs back to the start.

mistakes.mistake: Bending at the hips on the way down
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep one straight line; bend the knees to shorten the lever if needed.

mistakes.mistake: Resting the neck on the bench
mistakes.fix: The upper back and shoulders carry the load; keep the neck relaxed.
Keep the ribs down and the pelvis tucked.
Stop where you can still control the line.

kinematics.norm: Legs to about vertical (about 90 degrees), then the hips open toward a straight line as the pelvis rises (clinical opinion)
Shoulders to toes close to straight, steep above the bench (clinical opinion)
Pelvis and low back well off the bench; the upper back is the pivot (clinical opinion)
Rigid body lowered slowly; long-lever trunk work loads the spine heavily (Axler and McGill 1997)
About 2 s up and 2.5-3 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Advanced: build up with lying leg raises, reverse crunches and hollow holds first.
Low back pain: avoid; the long lever loads the spine heavily (Axler and McGill 1997).
Neck pain: stop; the weight should rest on the upper back and shoulders, not the neck.
Use a stable bench that will not tip.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and transversus keep the body in one rigid line as it lowers; the main load of the lift.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Lift the legs to vertical and help hold the line.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Lift the legs to vertical and help hold the line.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Brace the trunk and keep it from twisting.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Brace the trunk and keep it from twisting.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keep the hips open (no pike) in the rigid line.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Keep the hips open (no pike) in the rigid line.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull on the bench behind the head and anchor the upper back.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull on the bench behind the head and anchor the upper back.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Long head helps pull the arms down against the bench.
